services.name: OpenAI API
services.description: OpenAI's managed API platform for its text, reasoning, image, audio, realtime, embedding, moderation, and related model families.
services.service_boundary: Represents the developer API platform, not ChatGPT, Codex, individual model releases, or Azure-hosted OpenAI models.
services.regional_controls: Eligible API organizations can configure project-level regional storage and, for supported regions, regional processing; eligibility and endpoint coverage vary.
services.retention_controls: API data is not used for model training unless the customer opts in. Default abuse-monitoring and application-state retention vary by endpoint; approved organizations can use Modified Abuse Monitoring or Zero Data Retention with documented feature limitations.
services.routing: Customers select models within OpenAI's catalog; the service is not a cross-provider routing layer.
services.customization: Fine-tuning and stored application resources are available for eligible models and endpoints, with separate retention behavior.
strengths: One first-party platform spans multiple modalities, realtime interaction, tools, batch processing, and model customization.
Project-level administration, data controls, and regional endpoints are documented in the API platform.
tradeoffs: Regional processing, Zero Data Retention, and some enterprise controls require eligibility and do not cover every endpoint or feature.
The service exposes OpenAI models rather than a vendor-neutral catalog.

services.name: Anthropic API
services.description: Anthropic's managed first-party API for Claude models, including Messages, streaming, prompt caching, files, and asynchronous message batches.
services.service_boundary: Represents Anthropic's direct commercial API, not Claude.ai, Claude Code, model access through Bedrock or Vertex AI, or individual Claude releases.
services.regional_controls: Commercial API access is limited to Anthropic's supported countries and regions; the reviewed direct-API sources do not establish customer-selected processing regions.
services.retention_controls: Standard API inputs and outputs are deleted from backend systems within 30 days, subject to policy-enforcement and legal exceptions. Approved enterprise API customers may receive Zero Data Retention, with documented exceptions for features such as files and some batch or caching behavior.
services.routing: Customers select Claude models within Anthropic's direct API; access to Claude through other cloud platforms is a separate inference-service boundary.
services.customization: The reviewed API emphasizes prompt caching, files, tools, and batch execution rather than customer-deployed model weights.
strengths: The direct Messages API provides a focused first-party contract for Claude capabilities.
Anthropic publishes separate commercial retention guidance and a documented enterprise Zero Data Retention boundary.
tradeoffs: The direct service is limited to Anthropic model families.
Zero Data Retention is approval-based and feature-specific exceptions still require review.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.description: AWS's managed foundation-model platform for invoking, customizing, evaluating, and governing Amazon and third-party models within AWS accounts and regions.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Amazon Bedrock inference platform, not Amazon's model families, SageMaker-hosted endpoints, Amazon Q, or Bedrock AgentCore.
services.regional_controls: Model, feature, and endpoint availability is region-specific. Inference profiles can route within a geography or globally, while single-region use and provisioned capacity have separate support matrices.
services.retention_controls: Data handling depends on the selected model, Bedrock feature, region, AWS account controls, and any applicable third-party model terms; cross-region profiles can change the processing locations involved.
services.routing: Bedrock inference profiles can route a selected model across supported AWS regions; this is regional capacity routing rather than arbitrary cross-model selection.
services.customization: Eligible base models can be customized, and imported or custom models use distinct identifiers and capacity requirements.
strengths: One AWS control plane covers models from several publishers, regional IAM boundaries, and multiple capacity modes.
Inference profiles and provisioned throughput support production capacity and residency choices.
tradeoffs: Availability and API compatibility vary by model, endpoint, feature, and AWS region.
Third-party models can add publisher-specific terms on top of the AWS agreement.

services.name: Vertex AI Generative AI
services.description: Google Cloud's managed generative-AI platform for accessing Google, partner, open, and customer-deployed models through Vertex AI and Model Garden.
services.service_boundary: Represents managed generative inference on Vertex AI, not Gemini Apps, Google AI Studio, individual Gemini releases, or the broader Vertex AI agent platform.
services.regional_controls: Availability, data residency, and processing location depend on the selected model, endpoint type, and Google Cloud region; serverless and self-deployed Model Garden paths have different boundaries.
services.retention_controls: Data governance follows the selected Vertex AI service, project configuration, model publisher, and Google Cloud terms; customers must review model- and feature-specific documentation rather than infer one platform-wide rule.
services.routing: The platform provides a common cloud control plane across model sources, but the reviewed service is not represented as an automatic latency- or price-based cross-provider router.
services.customization: Model Garden supports managed APIs, tuning, and deployment paths for eligible Google, partner, open, and customer models, including dedicated endpoints for self-deployed models.
strengths: Model Garden combines first-party, partner, open, and customer deployment paths with Google Cloud governance.
Serverless, provisioned, batch, and dedicated deployment choices cover distinct production needs.
tradeoffs: Serving mode, region support, terms, and operational responsibility differ substantially across model categories.
The broad platform boundary requires model-specific review before treating any capability as universal.

evidence.label: Generative AI on Vertex AI overview

services.name: OpenRouter
services.description: A unified API and billing layer that routes model requests across multiple upstream inference providers and model publishers.
services.service_boundary: Represents OpenRouter's API routing service, not the upstream providers, the underlying model releases, or OpenRouter's end-user chat interface.
services.regional_controls: Enterprise customers can use documented EU in-region routing; provider and endpoint selection otherwise determines where upstream processing occurs.
services.retention_controls: OpenRouter documents opt-in prompt logging and per-request controls that restrict routing by upstream retention or data-collection policy; upstream provider behavior remains part of the effective boundary.
services.routing: Requests can use ordered providers, fallbacks, allowlists, denylists, privacy requirements, price ceilings, and latency or throughput preferences.
services.customization: The public service focuses on routing existing models and provider endpoints; private customer endpoints are documented separately as an enterprise beta and are not treated as a stable catalog capability here.
strengths: A single compatible API can express fallback, cost, latency, throughput, and data-policy constraints across providers.
Endpoint-level retention metadata makes privacy part of routing rather than a provider-wide assumption.
tradeoffs: Requests cross an additional service boundary before reaching an upstream inference provider.
Effective terms, availability, and data handling depend on both OpenRouter and the selected upstream endpoint.

services.name: GroqCloud
services.description: Groq's managed inference service for a selected production and preview catalog of openly available text, audio, safety, and compound AI models and systems.
services.service_boundary: Represents the GroqCloud developer API, not GroqChat, Groq Playground, Groq hardware, individual hosted models, or third-party model publishers.
services.regional_controls: Reviewed documentation states that retained customer data is stored in United States Google Cloud buckets; the pilot does not claim customer-selected inference regions.
services.retention_controls: Inference inputs and outputs are not retained by default except for reliability or abuse handling; customers can enable Zero Data Retention. Batch, fine-tuning, and other stateful features have separate retention behavior.
services.routing: Customers select among models hosted by Groq; Flex processing changes capacity behavior but is not a multi-provider routing layer.
services.customization: Fine-tuning and LoRA state are documented as retained until customer deletion; support and availability remain model-specific.
strengths: The service documents production versus preview models, token-speed signals, and OpenAI-compatible access.
On-demand, Flex, and batch paths expose distinct capacity and workload tradeoffs.
tradeoffs: The hosted catalog is selective and preview models may be discontinued on short notice.
Regional choice is narrower than multi-region cloud platforms in the reviewed documentation.

services.name: Gemini API
services.description: Google's direct developer API for Gemini generation, embeddings, media, tools, caching, files, and batch workloads.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Gemini API reached through Google AI Studio credentials, not Gemini Apps, Vertex AI, individual Gemini releases, or Google Cloud-hosted partner models.
services.regional_controls: The direct API is a global developer service; customer-selected Google Cloud regions and residency controls belong to the separate Vertex AI boundary.
services.retention_controls: Data use and logging depend on whether access is through paid services and on enabled features; customers must review the current Gemini API additional terms and feature-specific storage behavior.
services.routing: Customers select models from Google's direct catalog; this is not a cross-provider router.
services.customization: The reviewed direct API supports prompting, caching, files, tools, and tuned-model features where documented, not customer-managed serving infrastructure.
strengths: Direct access to Google's multimodal model APIs and developer tooling.
Native and OpenAI-compatible integration paths are documented.
tradeoffs: Its governance boundary differs from Vertex AI.
Feature availability and data behavior vary across free, paid, and stateful features.

services.name: xAI API
services.description: xAI's direct managed API for Grok models, multimodal generation, realtime features, and server-side search tools.
services.service_boundary: Represents api.x.ai, not the Grok consumer applications, X, Grok Build, individual model releases, or Grok served through another cloud platform.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed public API documentation centers on global endpoints; enterprise regional arrangements require contract review.
services.retention_controls: By default API requests and responses are retained for 30 days for abuse auditing and are not used for training without permission. Team-level Zero Data Retention is available with documented exclusions for stateful, file, collection, and batch features.
services.routing: Customers choose Grok models and optional xAI-operated tools; the service does not route across independent inference providers.
services.customization: The public API emphasizes model and tool invocation rather than imported customer weights.
strengths: Direct API access to Grok models and xAI-operated web and X search tools.
Self-service Zero Data Retention behavior is documented.
tradeoffs: The catalog is limited to xAI-operated models and tools.
Zero Data Retention disables several stateful API features.

services.name: Mistral AI Studio
services.description: Mistral AI's managed developer platform and API for its model families, embeddings, OCR, audio, agents, and related services.
services.service_boundary: Represents Mistral AI Studio, formerly La Plateforme, not Le Chat, open-weight downloads, self-deployed models, or partner-served Mistral endpoints.
services.regional_controls: Deployment and residency commitments vary between the hosted platform, enterprise arrangements, and partner-served deployments; the reviewed public docs do not support one universal region claim.
services.retention_controls: Data handling depends on account tier, feature, and governing commercial terms; stateful platform features must be reviewed separately from stateless model calls.
services.routing: Customers select models in the Mistral-hosted catalog; partner-served deployments are a distinct contractual path.
services.customization: Fine-tuning and agent-building paths are documented for eligible models and accounts.
strengths: A European-operated direct platform spans proprietary and open model families.
The platform includes model APIs, tuning, OCR, audio, and agent services.
tradeoffs: The broad platform includes features with different storage behavior.
Partner-hosted and customer-infrastructure deployments have separate terms and boundaries.

services.name: Cohere API
services.description: Cohere's direct API platform for Command generation, Embed, Rerank, classification, and enterprise language-model workflows.
services.service_boundary: Represents Cohere's hosted SaaS API, not Cohere models served by Oracle, Bedrock, Azure, or another partner and not private customer-infrastructure deployments.
services.regional_controls: Private and partner deployments may provide different residency controls; the public direct-API docs do not establish one customer-selected regional endpoint model.
services.retention_controls: Enterprise data commitments and account agreements govern input, output, and training-data handling; production customers should verify the applicable hosted-platform retention configuration.
services.routing: Customers select Cohere models and task APIs rather than upstream inference providers.
services.customization: Fine-tuning and private deployment options are available under separate eligibility and deployment paths.
strengths: First-party generation, embedding, and reranking APIs share one enterprise-oriented platform.
The service supports retrieval-heavy application patterns beyond generation alone.
tradeoffs: Deployment and data commitments differ between trial, production, private, and partner paths.
The direct catalog is Cohere-centered rather than vendor-neutral.

services.name: DeepSeek API
services.description: DeepSeek's direct managed API for its chat and reasoning model families through documented compatible interfaces.
services.service_boundary: Represents the DeepSeek Open Platform API, not the DeepSeek chat product, downloadable model weights, or DeepSeek models hosted by third parties.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed public documentation exposes a global API base URL and does not establish customer-selected inference regions.
services.retention_controls: The platform terms and privacy materials govern service data; the reviewed technical docs document request isolation but do not establish a universal Zero Data Retention option.
services.routing: Customers select DeepSeek-operated model endpoints; compatible interfaces do not make the service a router.
services.customization: The reviewed public direct API does not document customer-imported weights or dedicated deployments.
strengths: Direct first-party access with widely used compatible API conventions.
Technical documentation identifies model versions, limits, and isolation behavior.
tradeoffs: Public regional and retention controls are less explicit than major cloud platforms.
The direct service is limited to DeepSeek model families.

terms.label: DeepSeek Open Platform Terms of Service

services.name: Moonshot AI Open Platform
services.description: Moonshot AI's direct developer platform for Kimi model APIs and related generation capabilities.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Moonshot AI Open Platform API, not the Kimi consumer application, downloadable Kimi weights, or third-party Kimi hosting.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed international platform documentation does not establish customer-selected processing regions.
services.retention_controls: Use is governed by the Open Platform model-use agreement and privacy materials; customers should verify current retention and training-use commitments for their account and endpoint.
services.routing: Customers select Moonshot-operated Kimi models rather than independent inference providers.
services.customization: The reviewed public API is a managed model-access service and does not establish imported customer-weight deployment.
strengths: Direct access to Moonshot's Kimi model family.
OpenAI-compatible access lowers integration friction.
tradeoffs: Public regional controls are not clearly exposed.
The service boundary differs from Kimi access through routers and other hosts.

terms.label: Moonshot Open Platform Model Use Agreement

services.name: Z.ai Model API
services.description: Z.ai's direct managed API for GLM text, reasoning, coding, vision, image, video, and related model capabilities.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Z.ai Model API operated through api.z.ai, not the Z.ai chat product, open-weight GLM releases, or GLM models hosted elsewhere.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed Model API documentation uses a common platform endpoint and does not establish customer-selected inference regions.
services.retention_controls: The API-specific terms govern submitted inputs and outputs; the reviewed public technical docs do not establish a universal customer-configurable retention tier.
services.routing: Customers select Z.ai model endpoints; OpenAI SDK compatibility is an interface choice, not cross-provider routing.
services.customization: The reviewed public Model API focuses on hosted models and does not establish customer-supplied weight deployment.
strengths: Direct access to the GLM family across several modalities.
Official examples document both native HTTP and OpenAI SDK access.
tradeoffs: Public regional and retention controls require further contract-level review.
The direct service is limited to Z.ai-operated model families.

terms.label: Z.ai Model API Terms of Use

services.name: AI21 Studio
services.description: AI21 Labs' direct developer API for Jamba language models and task-oriented language services.
services.service_boundary: Represents AI21 Studio's direct API, not AI21 models served through Bedrock or other platforms and not AI21's end-user applications.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed public direct-API documentation does not establish customer-selected processing regions.
services.retention_controls: Data handling follows AI21's service terms and enterprise arrangements; stateful or batch features require feature-specific review.
services.routing: Customers select AI21-operated models rather than upstream providers.
services.customization: Customization and enterprise deployment options are eligibility- and contract-dependent.
strengths: Direct access to AI21's first-party language models.
Official compatibility guidance supports common client conventions.
tradeoffs: The direct catalog is narrower than multi-publisher clouds.
Public residency details are limited.

services.name: MiniMax Open Platform
services.description: MiniMax's international developer platform for language, speech, image, music, and video model APIs.
services.service_boundary: Represents the international MiniMax Open Platform API, not MiniMax consumer applications, mainland-China endpoints, or MiniMax models hosted by third parties.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed international documentation does not establish customer-selected processing regions.
services.retention_controls: Data handling follows the platform terms and API privacy policy; customers should review capability-specific rules for uploaded and generated media.
services.routing: Customers select MiniMax-operated models across supported modalities.
services.customization: The reviewed public API focuses on managed capability endpoints rather than customer-supplied model deployment.
strengths: A single direct platform spans several generative media modalities.
Official documentation provides native and compatible integration guidance.
tradeoffs: Media APIs introduce capability-specific storage and rights considerations.
Public regional-control documentation is limited.

terms.label: MiniMax Open Platform Terms of Service

services.name: Perplexity API
services.description: Perplexity's developer API for search-grounded answers, research workflows, and supported model invocation.
services.service_boundary: Represents Perplexity's developer API, not the Perplexity answer engine, Comet, Perplexity Computer, or third-party access to similarly named models.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed public API documentation does not establish customer-selected processing regions.
services.retention_controls: API-specific terms and product documentation govern request data; search and research features add external-source retrieval to the processing boundary.
services.routing: The service can combine model inference with Perplexity-operated search and research, but it is not represented here as a general-purpose provider router.
services.customization: The service exposes search, research, and model parameters rather than customer-imported model serving.
strengths: Search-grounded APIs combine inference with web retrieval and citations.
Compatibility endpoints support common integration patterns.
tradeoffs: Search-grounded requests have a broader data and source boundary than raw generation.
Regional controls are not prominent in the public docs.

services.name: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio
services.description: Alibaba Cloud's managed generative-AI platform for Qwen and third-party models, tuning, applications, and model APIs.
services.service_boundary: Represents Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, not the Qwen model family, Qwen Chat, downloadable weights, or Alibaba Cloud's broader machine-learning platform.
services.regional_controls: Keys, endpoints, model availability, storage, and inference deployment are region-scoped. Alibaba documents China and international regions plus Global, US, and EU deployment scopes with model-specific availability.
services.retention_controls: Alibaba states Model Studio data is not used for model training; stored resources and playground history have feature-specific behavior and remain region-dependent.
services.routing: Customers select models and region-scoped endpoints; compatible protocols do not imply automatic cross-provider routing.
services.customization: The platform supports tuning, application building, and deployment paths for eligible models and customer artifacts.
strengths: Broad access to Qwen and other models through region-scoped cloud controls.
OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible protocols are documented.
tradeoffs: Model and feature availability vary substantially by region.
The platform's broad scope requires model-specific terms and deployment review.

terms.label: Alibaba Cloud Product Terms of Service

services.name: Baidu Qianfan ModelBuilder
services.description: Baidu AI Cloud's managed foundation-model platform for ERNIE and third-party models, tuning, evaluation, and deployed inference services.
services.service_boundary: Represents Qianfan ModelBuilder, not the ERNIE model family, consumer chat products, Qianfan AppBuilder, or generic Baidu AI APIs.
services.regional_controls: International and mainland-China service paths and terms differ; endpoint and deployment availability must be verified for the selected Baidu Cloud region.
services.retention_controls: The Qianfan user agreement and applicable Baidu Cloud policies govern platform data; model, training, and deployed-service paths have distinct storage behavior.
services.routing: The platform exposes multiple models and deployment options but is not documented here as an automatic price- or latency-based upstream router.
services.customization: Qianfan supports data management, training, tuning, model management, and cloud deployment of inference services.
strengths: Combines Baidu's first-party models with third-party and open-model services.
Provides an end-to-end enterprise model development and serving path.
tradeoffs: International and mainland service boundaries differ.
Most detailed operational documentation is Chinese-language and feature-specific.

services.name: BytePlus ModelArk
services.description: BytePlus's managed model platform for Seed models and selected third-party models, online and batch inference, tuning, and endpoints.
services.service_boundary: Represents the international BytePlus ModelArk service, not mainland-China Volcengine Ark, ByteDance consumer products, individual Seed models, or Coding Plan subscriptions.
services.regional_controls: ModelArk documents AP and EU regions with region-isolated keys and endpoints. Some traffic may spill between the AP and EU service regions depending on the selected availability mode, so residency claims require endpoint-specific review.
services.retention_controls: Data processing and retention follow ModelArk-specific terms and the selected capability; batch, tuning, and dataset features have separate stateful boundaries.
services.routing: Customers choose models and region-scoped endpoints; documented availability spillover is infrastructure routing rather than arbitrary model routing.
services.customization: Tuning, datasets, online endpoints, and batch inference are documented, with capability differences by region.
strengths: International AP and EU endpoints are explicitly documented.
The service spans first-party Seed models and broader managed model workflows.
tradeoffs: EU feature and model coverage is narrower than AP coverage.
Cross-region spillover behavior must be checked for residency-sensitive workloads.

services.name: Microsoft Foundry Models
services.description: Azure's managed foundation-model catalog and inference platform for Azure Direct Models, partner models, open models, and customer deployments.
services.service_boundary: Represents model inference and deployment in Microsoft Foundry, including Azure OpenAI as an Azure-hosted path, not the direct OpenAI API, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or the broader Foundry agent platform.
services.regional_controls: Standard, Global, and Data Zone deployments have different processing boundaries. Geography-scoped and EU, US, or APAC Data Zone options are model- and deployment-specific.
services.retention_controls: Microsoft states Azure Direct Model prompts and outputs are not shared with model providers or used to train foundation models without permission; stateful APIs, batch, files, and abuse monitoring have separate storage behavior.
services.routing: Global and Data Zone deployment types can route capacity across allowed Azure locations for the selected model; this is cloud-capacity routing, not general provider selection.
services.customization: Fine-tuning, provisioned deployments, managed compute, and customer model deployments are available for eligible models.
strengths: A large multi-publisher catalog is integrated with Azure identity, networking, and geography controls.
Common inference APIs reduce integration differences across supported models.
tradeoffs: Model availability, terms, and processing geography vary by deployment type.
The product boundary and naming evolve quickly and require careful distinction from direct vendor APIs.

services.name: OCI Generative AI
services.description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's managed platform for first- and third-party foundation models, imported models, fine-tuning, and dedicated AI clusters.
services.service_boundary: Represents OCI Generative AI, not Oracle Database AI features, OCI Data Science model deployments, individual partner models, or those vendors' direct APIs.
services.regional_controls: Models, on-demand access, imported-model support, and dedicated cluster shapes are region-specific OCI resources.
services.retention_controls: Oracle documents that stateless inference inputs and outputs are not retained by OCI Generative AI. Projects and agent-related state expose separate configurable retention for responses and conversations.
services.routing: Customers select models and OCI regions; the platform does not present automatic cross-provider routing as its primary contract.
services.customization: Fine-tuned and imported models can run on dedicated AI clusters with customer-tenancy controls.
strengths: On-demand and dedicated serving coexist with imported-model and fine-tuning paths.
Oracle publishes explicit stateless inference data-handling guidance.
tradeoffs: Model and capacity support varies by OCI region.
Dedicated clusters require commitments and service-limit planning.

services.name: Databricks Foundation Model APIs
services.description: Databricks' managed foundation-model serving layer for pay-per-token, priority, provisioned-throughput, batch, and customer-model workloads.
services.service_boundary: Represents Databricks-hosted Foundation Model APIs and serving endpoints, not external-model credentials merely governed through Unity AI Gateway, MLflow alone, or model publishers' direct APIs.
services.regional_controls: Databricks documents region-specific model availability and treats Foundation Model APIs as a Designated Service using Databricks Geos for processing residency.
services.retention_controls: Logging and data processing follow workspace, serving-endpoint, and Databricks Geo controls; externally hosted models remain a separate downstream data boundary.
services.routing: Unity AI Gateway can apply governance across hosted and external model endpoints; this record's managed-host boundary covers Databricks-served models and endpoints.
services.customization: Provisioned throughput supports fine-tuned variants, supported architectures, and customer model weights registered through Unity Catalog.
strengths: Inference integrates with Unity Catalog governance and Databricks data workflows.
Pay-per-token, priority, provisioned, and batch modes cover distinct workloads.
tradeoffs: Capabilities and model catalogs differ across AWS, Azure, GCP, and regions.
External model routing can add separate provider terms beyond the hosted-service boundary.

services.name: IBM watsonx.ai Runtime
services.description: IBM's managed foundation-model inference and deployment runtime for IBM Granite, third-party, open, and customer models.
services.service_boundary: Represents model inference and deployments in watsonx.ai Runtime, not watsonx Assistant, watsonx.data, individual Granite releases, or models hosted outside IBM Cloud.
services.regional_controls: IBM Cloud service instances, supported models, and deployment spaces are region-specific; availability depends on the selected IBM Cloud location.
services.retention_controls: Data handling follows IBM Cloud terms, account controls, and the selected foundation-model or deployment feature; stored assets and stateless calls have distinct boundaries.
services.routing: Customers select foundation models or deployed assets in IBM Cloud rather than automatic upstream-provider routing.
services.customization: Prompt tuning, fine-tuning, custom foundation models, and deployment spaces are available for supported workflows.
strengths: IBM Granite and third-party models integrate with IBM Cloud governance and deployment spaces.
The service covers hosted APIs and customer deployment workflows.
tradeoffs: Availability and feature support vary by region and cloud plan.
The API surface spans several watsonx resource types rather than one universal endpoint.

services.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
services.description: Cloudflare's serverless inference platform for a selected catalog of open models deployed across Cloudflare's network.
services.service_boundary: Represents Workers AI inference, not Cloudflare AI Gateway, Vectorize, Workers runtime generally, model publishers, or customer-hosted GPU infrastructure.
services.regional_controls: Inference runs on Cloudflare's distributed network; the reviewed public product is not represented as a customer-selected single-region endpoint service.
services.retention_controls: Cloudflare's developer-platform terms and Workers AI data guidance govern request handling; AI Gateway logging is a separate optional service boundary.
services.routing: Customers select models from the Workers AI catalog; AI Gateway provider routing is a separate product.
services.customization: Fine-tunes and model catalog features are model-specific; arbitrary customer weight deployment is not claimed here.
strengths: Inference can be invoked directly from Cloudflare Workers near application logic.
A serverless API removes endpoint-capacity management for supported models.
tradeoffs: The model catalog is curated rather than arbitrary.
Distributed execution is different from fixed-region residency.

services.name: Tencent Cloud TokenHub
services.description: Tencent Cloud's Model-as-a-Service platform for Hunyuan, third-party proprietary, and open models with manual and automatic model selection modes.
services.service_boundary: Represents the current Tencent Cloud TokenHub service, not the deprecated Hunyuan and LLM Knowledge Engine sales paths, Tencent consumer products, TI-ONE, or individual model publishers.
services.regional_controls: Tencent documents separate Singapore global, Guangzhou mainland-China, and Silicon Valley US API addresses and scheduling scopes.
services.retention_controls: TokenHub terms authorize Tencent and applicable third-party model providers to process user inputs; effective retention depends on the selected model, operational mode, and applicable provider terms.
services.routing: Manual mode uses a customer-selected model. Auto Mode for eligible plans selects a model based on the input; third-party models can be reached through Tencent as an intermediary.
services.customization: The platform documents pay-as-you-go, guaranteed resources, and exclusive deployment; availability is model- and region-specific.
strengths: A current unified Tencent Cloud service spans Hunyuan and several major third-party model families.
Official docs expose regional endpoints and automatic model-selection behavior.
tradeoffs: Third-party models add publisher-specific terms and downstream processing boundaries.
The predecessor APIs are being migrated, so integrations must target the current TokenHub endpoints.

terms.label: LLM Service TokenHub Terms of Service

services.name: NVIDIA API Catalog
services.description: NVIDIA's hosted evaluation and developer API catalog for NIM inference microservices running on NVIDIA-managed DGX Cloud infrastructure.
services.service_boundary: Represents hosted APIs invoked from NVIDIA's API Catalog, not self-hosted NIM containers, NVIDIA hardware, downloadable model artifacts, or cloud partners operating their own NIM endpoints.
services.regional_controls: The hosted catalog documentation does not present customer-selected inference regions; production residency controls differ for self-hosted and partner-hosted NIM deployments.
services.retention_controls: Hosted API use follows NVIDIA API trial and service terms; model-specific and preview conditions must be reviewed before production use.
services.routing: Customers invoke a selected hosted NIM endpoint; the catalog is not a general automatic multi-provider router.
services.customization: Portable NIM microservices can be deployed elsewhere, but that customer- or partner-hosted path is outside this hosted-service record.
strengths: A broad multimodal catalog exposes documented APIs backed by NVIDIA's inference stack.
The same NIM packaging concept supports later migration to controlled deployments.
tradeoffs: Catalog-hosted endpoints and self-hosted NIM are materially different service boundaries.
Hosted catalog access may be evaluation-oriented or subject to model-specific availability.

services.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
services.description: Hugging Face's unified proxy, authentication, and billing layer for hundreds of models served by integrated inference providers.
services.service_boundary: Represents routed Inference Providers requests, not dedicated Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, the Hub model repository, local inference, or the upstream providers themselves.
services.regional_controls: Processing location depends on the selected upstream provider and model; the proxy does not establish one universal Hugging Face inference region.
services.retention_controls: Requests traverse Hugging Face proxy infrastructure and the selected provider unless a custom provider key path states otherwise; both layers' data policies apply.
services.routing: Automatic selection can prefer fastest, cheapest, or user-preferred providers and can fail over when a provider is unavailable; callers can also name a provider explicitly.
services.customization: The service routes existing provider-model combinations and is not a customer-weight deployment product.
strengths: One token and client can access many integrated providers and models.
Explicit fastest, cheapest, preferred, and provider-specific selection policies are documented.
tradeoffs: Requests add a proxy boundary and may reach different upstream operators.
Residency, retention, capabilities, and availability remain provider-specific.

services.name: Hugging Face Inference Endpoints
services.description: Hugging Face's managed dedicated and autoscaling deployment service for models and custom handlers sourced from Hub repositories.
services.service_boundary: Represents customer-created Inference Endpoints, not Inference Providers routing, the Hub repository alone, Spaces, or self-hosted inference engines.
services.regional_controls: Customers choose among documented AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud regions and instance types; private connectivity support is provider- and region-specific.
services.retention_controls: Hugging Face states it does not store endpoint request payloads or tokens and retains service logs for 30 days. Uploaded model repositories and deployment resources remain stored customer assets.
services.routing: Traffic targets a customer-created endpoint and its autoscaling replicas rather than an external provider-selection layer.
services.customization: Customers choose model repositories, revisions, inference engines, containers, hardware, scaling, and custom handlers.
strengths: Dedicated model deployments combine Hub artifacts with managed infrastructure and autoscaling.
Cloud, region, hardware, access, and private-network choices are explicit.
tradeoffs: Customers retain more deployment and model-compatibility responsibility than serverless catalogs.
Available regions and private connectivity differ by underlying cloud.

services.name: Together AI
services.description: Together AI's managed inference platform for serverless and dedicated access to open and selected proprietary models.
services.service_boundary: Represents Together's hosted inference APIs and dedicated endpoints, not model publishers, the Together research organization, or customer-operated inference software.
services.regional_controls: Dedicated deployment and enterprise arrangements can define infrastructure placement; the public serverless catalog does not establish customer-selected regions for every model.
services.retention_controls: Data handling follows Together's terms and the selected serverless, batch, fine-tuning, or dedicated feature; stateful artifacts have separate lifecycles.
services.routing: Customers choose a hosted model or endpoint; the platform is not primarily an automatic cross-provider router.
services.customization: Fine-tuning, LoRA, dedicated endpoints, and customer model deployment are available for supported architectures.
strengths: Serverless and dedicated paths cover experimentation through reserved production capacity.
A broad open-model catalog uses a common compatible API.
tradeoffs: Catalog, lifecycle, and capacity guarantees differ between serverless and dedicated modes.
Model terms remain publisher-specific.

services.name: Fireworks AI
services.description: Fireworks AI's managed inference platform for serverless models, on-demand and reserved deployments, fine-tuning, and batch workloads.
services.service_boundary: Represents Fireworks-hosted model APIs and deployments, not model publishers, Fireworks client libraries, or customer-operated inference runtimes.
services.regional_controls: Regional and private deployment options are enterprise- and deployment-specific; public serverless placement is not universally customer-selected.
services.retention_controls: Data handling follows Fireworks terms and feature-specific behavior for serverless inference, batch files, fine-tunes, and deployments.
services.routing: Customers select a model or deployment; Fireworks manages serving capacity rather than routing to unrelated upstream providers.
services.customization: Fine-tuning, LoRA, custom models, and dedicated deployments are documented for supported formats.
strengths: Multiple capacity modes support both bursty and predictable workloads.
OpenAI-compatible APIs cover a broad hosted model catalog.
tradeoffs: Production controls depend on deployment tier and contract.
Publisher terms and model lifecycle remain model-specific.

services.name: Cerebras Inference
services.description: Cerebras's managed high-throughput inference API for a selected catalog of open models plus enterprise dedicated endpoints.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Cerebras hosted inference service, not Cerebras hardware systems, downloadable models, or customer-operated Cerebras deployments.
services.regional_controls: The shared API does not expose customer-selected regions in the reviewed docs; enterprise dedicated endpoints define separate capacity and placement arrangements.
services.retention_controls: Batch input files and results default to seven-day retention; prompt caches are ephemeral. Other request and logging behavior follows the service agreement and feature documentation.
services.routing: Customers select a hosted model or dedicated endpoint; service tiers affect admission priority rather than upstream-provider selection.
services.customization: Enterprise plans document fine-tuned models, uploaded model versions, and dedicated endpoints.
strengths: The service is optimized for high token throughput on Cerebras infrastructure.
Shared, batch, priority, and dedicated paths are documented.
tradeoffs: The shared production catalog is selective.
Regional placement and custom endpoints require enterprise coordination.

services.name: SambaNova Cloud
services.description: SambaNova's hosted inference API for selected open models on SambaNova dataflow infrastructure.
services.service_boundary: Represents SambaNova Cloud's developer API, not SambaNova on-premises systems, model publishers, or third-party gateways exposing SambaNova endpoints.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed public cloud documentation does not establish customer-selected inference regions; private and on-premises offerings are separate boundaries.
services.retention_controls: Request handling follows SambaNova's cloud terms and account arrangements; the reviewed public docs do not support a universal configurable retention claim.
services.routing: Customers select models hosted by SambaNova rather than unrelated upstream providers.
services.customization: Reserved and private capacity arrangements are enterprise paths; arbitrary public customer-weight upload is not claimed here.
strengths: OpenAI-compatible access simplifies adoption of its hosted model catalog.
SambaNova-operated infrastructure provides a distinct accelerator path.
tradeoffs: The hosted catalog and public regional controls are limited compared with hyperscale clouds.
Private deployment capabilities belong to separate commercial arrangements.

services.name: DeepInfra
services.description: DeepInfra's serverless and dedicated managed inference service for text, embeddings, reranking, image, audio, and other open models.
services.service_boundary: Represents DeepInfra-hosted APIs and deployments, not model publishers, client libraries, or customer-operated copies of the same weights.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed serverless documentation does not establish customer-selected regions for every model; dedicated deployment placement requires plan-specific review.
services.retention_controls: Data handling follows DeepInfra's terms and privacy documentation; dedicated and serverless logging behavior should be verified separately.
services.routing: Customers select a DeepInfra-hosted model or endpoint rather than upstream inference providers.
services.customization: Dedicated deployments and custom model hosting are available for supported artifacts.
strengths: A broad open-model catalog is available through compatible and task-specific APIs.
Serverless and dedicated paths address different capacity needs.
tradeoffs: Catalog lifecycle follows upstream model availability.
Enterprise regional and retention controls require plan-specific confirmation.

services.name: Replicate
services.description: Replicate's managed API and deployment platform for running public, private, and customer-packaged machine-learning models.
services.service_boundary: Represents Replicate's hosted prediction and deployment service, not model authors, the open-source Cog packaging tool alone, or deployments run outside Replicate.
services.regional_controls: Public models run on Replicate-managed infrastructure; deployment and enterprise location options require service-specific review rather than a universal region claim.
services.retention_controls: Prediction inputs, outputs, files, and logs have documented lifecycle behavior that varies by API object and deployment; sensitive workloads require those feature rules to be reviewed.
services.routing: Predictions target a named model version or deployment; Replicate manages hardware scheduling rather than routing across external providers.
services.customization: Customers can package models with Cog, push private models, and create deployments with chosen hardware and scaling settings.
strengths: A large cross-modal model catalog shares a consistent prediction lifecycle.
Custom model packaging and managed deployments are first-class paths.
tradeoffs: Individual public models differ in ownership, terms, interface, and maintenance.
Prediction artifacts and asynchronous workflows require explicit retention review.

services.name: Venice API
services.description: Venice.ai's cross-modal inference API for private and anonymized access to open-weight and proprietary text, image, video, audio, embedding, and related models.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Venice developer API and its decentralized or upstream inference routing, not the Venice.ai end-user assistant, upstream model publishers, or customer-operated model deployments.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed public documentation does not establish customer-selected processing regions; private models run across Venice's decentralized provider fleet, while anonymized models can reach third-party frontier providers.
services.retention_controls: Venice states that it does not store or log API prompts or model responses. Effective privacy still depends on the selected model tier: private models use Venice-routed GPU capacity, while anonymized frontier models are proxied to third parties under different upstream handling, and selected models offer TEE or client-side E2EE.
services.routing: Customers select models from a cross-provider catalog. Venice routes private requests across decentralized GPU providers and proxies anonymized requests to frontier providers; response headers can identify the model and router when available.
services.customization: The service exposes model selection, system-prompt behavior, tools, structured output, and modality-specific generation parameters; arbitrary customer-weight deployment is not established as a public API capability.
strengths: One compatible API spans a large cross-provider and cross-modal model catalog.
Per-model privacy labels plus TEE and E2EE options make inference-boundary differences unusually visible.
tradeoffs: Private and anonymized model modes have materially different upstream boundaries and privacy properties.
The broad, frequently changing catalog requires model-level capability, terms, and retention review.

services.name: Stability AI Developer Platform
services.description: Stability AI's first-party managed API for generating, editing, controlling, and upscaling images with Stable Image and related creative models.
services.service_boundary: Represents the managed Stability AI API, not Stable Assistant, DreamStudio, downloadable model weights, model licenses, or separately contracted on-premises and self-hosted enterprise deployments.
services.regional_controls: The reviewed public API documentation does not establish customer-selected processing regions; on-premises and self-hosted enterprise options are separate deployment boundaries.
services.retention_controls: Inputs, outputs, account data, moderation, and service telemetry are governed by Stability AI's current terms and privacy policy; the reviewed API docs do not support a universal customer-configurable zero-retention claim.
services.routing: Customers call named Stability endpoints and models; the service is not a cross-provider router.
services.customization: API parameters cover generation, image-to-image, masks, structure and style control, background and object edits, relighting, and several upscale modes. Enterprise self-hosting is documented separately from the managed API.
strengths: A focused first-party API exposes a deep set of image generation, control, editing, and upscale operations.
Synchronous and asynchronous REST workflows cover both interactive transforms and heavier creative operations.
tradeoffs: The API is specialized for creative media rather than a general text or agent inference catalog.
Public regional and retention controls are less explicit than the feature-level image documentation.

services.name: Ollama Cloud
services.description: Managed hosting for open-weight models that Ollama clients can call in place of local execution, reachable through a local Ollama host or directly on ollama.com.
services.service_boundary: Represents the hosted service operated by Ollama. The self-operated Ollama runtime is a separate local-runtime record, and the models offered through the service remain their publishers' artifacts.
services.regional_controls: Ollama states that it hosts models and compute primarily in the United States and may route to Europe and Singapore for additional capacity. Customers are not offered a documented region selection or residency guarantee.
services.retention_controls: Ollama states that prompt and response data is never logged or trained on, that it requires no-logging, no-training, zero-retention terms from its hosting partners, and that zero data retention and logging is a plan feature. Its terms of service state that inputs and outputs are not used to train models.
services.routing: Requests are served from Ollama's own capacity across its partner providers; the service is not a cross-provider routing layer and does not expose routing policy to the customer.
services.customization: The service exposes a curated cloud model library. No fine-tuning, customer-supplied weights, or dedicated deployment path is documented.
strengths: Cloud models are addressed through the same client, CLI, and API surface as local models, so a local workflow moves to hosted capacity without rewriting the integration.
Retention posture is stated plainly, including a contractual no-logging, no-training, zero-retention requirement on hosting partners.
tradeoffs: Processing geography is described rather than selected; there is no documented region pinning or residency commitment.
The service offers on-demand capacity only, with no documented batch, reserved, or dedicated path and no customer-supplied models.
The catalogue is a curated set of cloud-enabled open-weight models rather than an open model marketplace.

evidence.label: Cloud service overview and data handling

services.name: Nebius Token Factory
services.description: Managed inference and post-training platform for open-weight models, offering shared endpoints, region-pinned dedicated endpoints, custom weight hosting, and fine-tuning.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Token Factory inference platform, previously presented as Nebius AI Studio. Nebius AI Cloud's general GPU compute and the models served through the platform remain separate boundaries.
services.regional_controls: Nebius describes data centres in Finland, France, and the United States and states that a dedicated endpoint processes requests only in the selected region, without multi-region routing or automatic overflow. It presents itself as an EU data processor operating under GDPR with a customer-facing data processing agreement.
services.retention_controls: Nebius documents an account-level zero-data-retention setting under which inputs and outputs are not stored after a request is processed, and describes itself as processor with the customer as controller for content submitted to inference endpoints.
services.routing: Shared endpoints are served from Nebius capacity with documented rate limits and scaling rules. Dedicated endpoints are explicitly not routed outside their configured region.
services.customization: Supervised fine-tuning, LoRA and full fine-tuning, adapter merging, custom speculators, and hosting of customer-supplied weights on dedicated endpoints are documented.
strengths: Dedicated endpoints pin processing to one selected region with an explicit statement that there is no multi-region overflow.
Customer-supplied weights, fine-tuning, and adapter lifecycle are first-class rather than adjacent products.
Inference observability and API integrations are documented as part of the service rather than left to the customer.
tradeoffs: The catalogue is open-weight models; first-party frontier models from other developers are not part of the boundary.
The service was recently renamed from Nebius AI Studio, so third-party references and older integration guides may not match current documentation.
Region pinning is documented for dedicated endpoints; shared-endpoint placement is not presented as customer-selected.

terms.label: Nebius Token Factory legal quick guide

services.name: Baseten
services.description: Managed inference platform offering hosted model APIs alongside dedicated deployments of open-source, fine-tuned, or customer-supplied models on autoscaled GPU capacity across several clouds and regions.
services.service_boundary: Represents Baseten's managed inference and training platform operated by Baseten Labs. The open-source packaging tooling it publishes and the models customers deploy remain separate boundaries.
services.regional_controls: Baseten documents multi-cloud capacity management across providers and regions, regional environments intended to satisfy data-residency requirements, private networking, and workload isolation. Specific region availability depends on the hosting option selected.
services.retention_controls: Baseten's terms make the customer the exclusive owner of its content, prohibit training on customer content, limit Baseten's own use to deidentified and aggregated statistics, and commit to destroying copies of customer content after a twenty-day retrieval window following termination.
services.routing: The platform provisions GPU capacity across clouds and regions and autoscales dedicated deployments; it is not a cross-provider model router and does not expose upstream provider selection.
services.customization: Dedicated deployment of open-source, fine-tuned, and custom models is a primary path, alongside supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning loops and training jobs on dedicated GPU clusters.
strengths: Hosted model APIs and dedicated deployment of customer-supplied models sit in one platform with a shared observability surface.
Terms are explicit that customer content is customer-owned, is not used for training, and is destroyed after a stated retrieval window.
Multi-cloud capacity management with regional environments and private networking addresses procurement and residency constraints directly.
tradeoffs: Region and capacity availability depend on the hosting option and provider mix rather than a single published region list.
The platform targets teams operating their own models; it is not a catalogue of third-party proprietary frontier models.
Anthropic Messages compatibility is documented as beta, so contract parity should be confirmed before relying on it.

services.name: Meta Model API
services.description: Meta's self-serve managed API for its hosted Muse model families, exposing OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible request formats over one inference pipeline.
services.service_boundary: Represents the developer inference API Meta operates at api.meta.ai, not the consumer Meta AI assistant, the Muse Code coding agent, individual Muse or Llama model releases, or open-weight Muse Glimmer running on customer hardware.
services.regional_controls: Availability is jurisdiction-gated by a dated Model Designation and Geographic Use Policy that names restricted territories and per-model country exclusions, and Meta may enable or restrict any jurisdiction at its discretion. Meta states it does not receive, determine, or route traffic based on end-user location, and no customer-selected processing region, regional endpoint, or private networking option is documented.
services.retention_controls: Data handling is tied to a published model tier rather than an account setting. Standard-tier models are processed under the Meta Global Processor Terms and are not used to train Meta models; the discounted Contributor tier grants Meta permission to train on prompts and completions, carries an instruction not to submit confidential or personal information, and offers no per-request opt-out. Meta retains content and usage data to deliver the service, meet legal obligations, exercise its rights, and run safety, abuse, and policy review; no zero-retention or customer deletion control is documented.
services.routing: Customers select a published Meta model id; the service exposes only Meta's own hosted models and performs no cross-provider routing or fallback.
services.customization: No fine-tuning, customer-supplied models, or dedicated deployments are documented. Lifecycle control is limited to pinning published checkpoint model ids and to prompt caching.
strengths: Three interchangeable request formats run the same models over one pipeline, so existing OpenAI or Anthropic client code ports with a base-URL and key change.
Training use is bound to an explicitly labelled model id and backed by processor terms, a data security addendum, and a published subprocessor list, rather than to an account toggle.
An unauthenticated status endpoint reports overall service state, per-model health, and recent incident history alongside documented retry guidance.
tradeoffs: The terms govern a limited preview period, and there is no batch, reserved-capacity, dedicated-endpoint, or fine-tuning path.
Regional control is a restriction list rather than a customer choice: no processing geography, regional endpoint, or private-network option is offered.
Only Meta's own hosted models are served, and account administration is limited to team-scoped API keys and shared rate limits with no documented SSO, audit logging, or service-level commitment.

services.name: Requesty
services.description: A routing API that forwards requests to several hundred hosted models through one compatible endpoint.
services.service_boundary: Represents Requesty's routing service, not the upstream providers it forwards to or the models they publish.
services.regional_controls: A European endpoint is documented on every plan, so requests can be kept within an EU routing path.
services.retention_controls: The privacy policy states that customer data is not used to train models and describes this as absolute on paid plans; logs are encrypted and held for up to thirty days, and a zero-retention mode disables logging. Models whose providers permit training are labelled and offered without charge.
services.routing: Routing policies cover fallback and load balancing across providers, with spend controls and guardrails including personal-data detection.
services.customization: The service routes existing hosted models; no customer fine-tuning or private model hosting is documented.
strengths: A European routing endpoint is offered on every plan rather than reserved for enterprise agreements.
Models whose providers permit training on inputs are labelled as such and offered at no cost, making that tradeoff explicit.
tradeoffs: The terms of service render only in a browser, so the governing text could not be read from the published page.
Documented model and provider counts differ between the vendor's own pages.
Requests cross an additional service boundary before reaching an upstream provider.

services.name: Eden AI
services.description: A French-operated API that forwards one request format to language, document, speech, translation, and vision models from many vendors.
services.service_boundary: Represents Eden AI's aggregation API across several model categories, not the upstream vendors it forwards to.
services.regional_controls: The operator is a French company and documents European data governance; upstream processing geography follows the selected provider.
services.retention_controls: The terms state customer data is not used to train models and that prompts and outputs are not stored by default, with limited billing metadata retained. The operator explicitly disclaims control over upstream providers' retention.
services.routing: Requests are directed to a selected vendor for a chosen capability, with fallback across vendors for the same task.
services.customization: The service focuses on aggregating existing vendor models across categories rather than customer fine-tuning.
strengths: Coverage extends past language models to document, speech, translation, and vision vendors through one contract and one request format.
The operator is a named French company with dated terms and a stated position on training and storage.
tradeoffs: Documented model and provider counts differ across the vendor's own pages.
Breadth across model categories means the effective data boundary varies by which vendor a request reaches.
Whether platform fees apply to customer-supplied provider keys is not documented.

services.name: AI/ML API
services.description: A hosted API that resells access to roughly a thousand text, image, video, and voice models at its own per-token rates.
services.service_boundary: Represents the AI/ML API reselling service, not the labs whose models it forwards to.
services.regional_controls: No customer control over processing geography is documented.
services.retention_controls: The privacy policy states no retention period beyond keeping data as long as necessary, and no position on training over customer prompts is documented.
services.routing: Requests reach a named model through one compatible endpoint; provider selection, fallback, and steering controls are not documented.
services.customization: No customer fine-tuning or private deployment is documented.
strengths: A single compatible endpoint reaches an unusually broad multimodal catalogue spanning text, image, video, and voice vendors.
Response headers report spend per request, making cost attribution possible without a separate metering system.
tradeoffs: Per-token rates are the operator's own and sit consistently above the rates other aggregators publish for the same models, with no statement anywhere of how they relate to upstream pricing.
The terms promise to carry a last-updated date and carry none, and no position on training over customer prompts is stated.
Subscription tiers and the paused free tier are visible only after signing in.

services.name: Nano-GPT
services.description: A routing API and chat surface reaching about a thousand text, image, video, and audio models, usable without an account.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Nano-GPT routing service and its chat surface, not the upstream providers it forwards to.
services.regional_controls: No customer control over processing geography is documented; provider selection determines where upstream processing occurs.
services.retention_controls: The terms state the operator is not authorised to train models on customer content, and chat history is held locally by default. The terms are unusually candid that zero-retention routing is a best-effort classification based on a provider's own claim rather than verified visibility into that provider's servers.
services.routing: Requests can be pinned to a chosen provider, and a broad set of upstream partners is named in the privacy policy.
services.customization: The service routes existing hosted models; no customer fine-tuning is documented.
strengths: Accountless and cryptocurrency-payable access, with generated user identifiers, removes the usual identity requirement for reaching hosted models.
The terms state plainly that zero-retention status is a provider claim rather than something the operator can verify, which most competitors assert without qualification.
Catalogue breadth spans text, image, video, and speech through one compatible endpoint.
tradeoffs: The operating company is registered but otherwise impersonal, with no named team, no funding disclosure, and an absent about page.
No control over processing geography is documented.
Confidence in retention behaviour rests on upstream provider claims by the operator's own admission.

services.name: Vercel AI Gateway
services.description: A routing service that forwards requests to hosted model providers at provider list price, with budgets scoped to teams and keys.
services.service_boundary: Represents Vercel's gateway service, not the upstream providers or Vercel's wider hosting platform.
services.regional_controls: No customer control over processing geography is documented for the gateway itself; upstream provider selection determines where processing occurs.
services.retention_controls: Zero-retention handling is documented both per request and as a chargeable team-wide setting, and customer-supplied provider keys are supported on paid plans.
services.routing: Requests can fall back across providers, and customer-supplied keys are used first with documented fallback to platform credentials when a key fails.
services.customization: The service routes existing hosted models; no customer fine-tuning or private model deployment is documented.
strengths: Documentation states plainly that no markup and no platform fee are applied to tokens, and dates itself, which is rare among comparable services.
Budgets can be scoped to a team, project, key, or member rather than only to an account.
Observability exports through open telemetry drains rather than a proprietary console only.
tradeoffs: A failed request using a customer-supplied key falls back to platform credentials and that usage is billed, so key failures carry a silent cost.
The free tier reaches a subset of the catalogue, and free credits stop applying permanently once credits are purchased.
Team-wide provider allowlisting and zero retention are billed per request, while their per-request equivalents are free.

services.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
services.description: A proxy that fronts requests to two dozen hosted model providers, adding caching, rate limiting, and analytics.
services.service_boundary: Represents Cloudflare's gateway product, not the upstream providers it fronts or Cloudflare's own model hosting.
services.regional_controls: Requests traverse the operator's global network; no gateway-level control over processing geography is documented.
services.retention_controls: Persistent log volumes differ by plan, and log forwarding is available on paid plans. Customer-supplied provider credentials can be stored so that the operator never holds the billing relationship.
services.routing: Caching, rate limiting, and request retry are configurable per gateway, and credential precedence runs from the request, to stored keys, to the operator's own billing.
services.customization: The gateway fronts existing provider APIs in their native formats; customer fine-tuning is not part of the product.
strengths: Core caching, rate limiting, and analytics are available without charge on a free account and require no infrastructure.
Customer-supplied provider credentials remove the operator from the billing path entirely.
Data-loss prevention scanning is available on all plans rather than reserved for paid tiers.
tradeoffs: Providers connect through their own native request formats, and a single compatible endpoint across providers could not be confirmed from the documentation.
Persistent log retention is capped far lower on the free tier, and forwarding logs elsewhere requires a paid plan.
Credits bought through the operator's unified billing carry a stated percentage fee, avoidable only by supplying provider keys.

services.name: Martian Gateway
services.description: A routing API forwarding to a few hundred hosted models, alongside a separately branded endpoint applying inference-time optimisation.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Martian routing gateway, not the operator's research work or the separately branded optimisation product sold under another name.
services.regional_controls: No customer control over processing geography is documented.
services.retention_controls: The terms grant the operator a sublicensable right to use customer materials, defined to include all input data, for purposes that expressly include training and improving the operator's own machine-learning models. No retention period is stated.
services.routing: Requests reach named models through one compatible endpoint; a separately branded endpoint applies inference-time optimisation to frontier models.
services.customization: Inference-time optimisation is sold as a distinct endpoint rather than as customer fine-tuning.
strengths: Inference-time optimisation is offered as a product with a stated quality commitment, which is a different proposition from routing alone.
The gateway exposes both compatible request formats and publishes a public model listing without requiring a key.
tradeoffs: The terms expressly license the operator to train its own models on customer inputs, which is the opposite of the default among comparable services.
The pricing page the operator's own contract cites does not exist, so the fee model cannot be established from published documents.
The product has been repositioned twice and now sits alongside a separately branded successor, leaving the durable boundary unclear.

services.name: Chutes
services.description: An inference platform serving open-weight models on a decentralised GPU network, which also runs customer-supplied model code.
services.service_boundary: Represents the Chutes hosting service, not the underlying decentralised network protocol or the open-weight models it serves.
services.regional_controls: Capacity comes from a decentralised operator network rather than named regions, and no customer control over processing geography is documented.
services.retention_controls: The terms state that API requests, responses, and application content are not used to train models, and that content is not logged for public inference. Customer-created deployments are noted as running code the operator does not control.
services.routing: Requests reach a named open-weight model on network capacity; private deployments run on dedicated hardware billed by time.
services.customization: Customers can deploy their own model code and weights as private endpoints on dedicated hardware.
strengths: Confidential-compute execution is marked on every model in the public catalogue rather than offered as a premium tier.
Capacity comes from a decentralised operator network rather than a single cloud, which changes the concentration risk profile.
The platform's own core is published under a permissive licence, which is uncommon among hosted inference operators.
tradeoffs: The catalogue is open-weight only, so it is not an alternative for reaching proprietary frontier models.
The operating entity is unclear, with no named legal company and a team page listing mostly handles.
A pricing path on the operator's own site returns a not-found body under a success status, which would mislead automated checks.

services.name: TrustedRouter
services.description: Routes requests to hundreds of models through one compatible endpoint, using hardware-attested gateways that log no prompt or output content.
services.service_boundary: Represents the TrustedRouter routing service and its attested gateway, not the upstream providers it forwards to. A small set of house composite models is layered over other providers' models rather than separately trained.
services.regional_controls: A European routing alias is documented alongside zero-retention and end-to-end aliases; upstream provider selection still determines where processing occurs.
services.retention_controls: The privacy policy states prompts and outputs are never logged, with an opt-in batch path retaining enclave-encrypted artifacts for up to thirty days. Request metadata is itemised but carries no fixed retention period. Upstream retention is disclaimed twice, and only a minority of catalogue models route to a zero-retention upstream.
services.routing: Aliases select automatic health-based failover, zero-retention routes, end-to-end encrypted routes, or European routes, and per-request constraints can require a minimum privacy class.
services.customization: Customer-supplied provider keys are supported on many models; no customer fine-tuning is documented, and the house models are ensembles over existing providers.
strengths: The privacy claim is cryptographically checkable rather than asserted: a live attestation signed by the cloud operator names an image digest matching the published one, and binds the connection's own certificate.
Three confidential-computing planes are documented, with signed trust artifacts recorded in a public transparency log.
Corporate identity is disclosed to an unusual degree, including registration identifiers and a named signatory, in a category where anonymous operators are common.
tradeoffs: The gateway and control plane are published under a source-available licence granting no production use for four years, so the service's own description of the code as fully open is inaccurate.
No third-party audit exists; the operator states its compliance certification is not obtained and its processing addendum is an unsigned draft.
Documented provider coverage is materially higher than the live catalogue supports, and most models do not route to a zero-retention upstream.
The operation rests on one named individual with no disclosed funding, and the trust page links a repository that does not exist.

services.name: Volcengine Ark
services.operator: 北京火山引擎科技有限公司 (Beijing Volcano Engine Technology)
services.description: ByteDance's mainland-China platform serving its own and third-party models with tuning, batch, reserved capacity, and dedicated endpoints.
services.service_boundary: Represents the mainland-China Volcengine Ark platform, whose licence limits use to mainland China, not the international BytePlus ModelArk service, ByteDance consumer products, or individual Doubao model releases.
services.regional_controls: All documented endpoints are in one mainland region and the platform terms grant a licence to use the service only within mainland China. Private network access is available through virtual-network endpoints without changing the request address.
services.retention_controls: Platform terms commit to not storing or training on customer data without separate consent, naming exceptions for compliance filtering, customer-requested troubleshooting, and abnormal-invocation alerts. A sandbox tier keeps data from reaching third-party model publishers, and customers may hold their own encryption keys. Individual-edition subscription plans reverse this default and authorise storage and training use of inputs and outputs, withdrawable only by leaving the plan.
services.routing: Customers select a model or endpoint identifier. A routing model can auto-select among a customer-scoped model set by prompt, quality, and cost preference, limited to the chat interface and shorter contexts. Reserved throughput takes priority and spills over to the shared pool.
services.customization: Supervised, preference, and continued-pretraining tuning with datasets and evaluation jobs; tuned and customer-uploaded open-weight models deploy on dedicated units, including quantised variants.
strengths: Platform terms state a no-storage, no-training default and enumerate each exception, with published and effective dates.
Four serving modes span shared on-demand, reserved throughput, dedicated units with elastic scaling, and discounted batch.
Serves first-party models alongside separately contracted third-party publishers and accepts customer-uploaded open-weight models.
tradeoffs: The service licence is restricted to mainland China and only one region is documented.
Individual-edition subscription plans authorise storage and training use of prompts and outputs, with no withdrawal short of leaving the plan.
Documentation is Chinese only and several catalogue pages return empty bodies over HTTP.
